llm.summary: This mobile-testing skill mostly matches its stated purpose, but setup can run unverified internet-downloaded code and privileged installers.

dimensions.detail: Booting emulators, running adb reverse, and executing Maestro tests are purpose-aligned, but executing a mutable remote installer locally and in the CI example is broader trust than the reviewed artifact can bound.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts/setup.sh instruct or perform curl from https://get.maestro.mobile.dev piped directly to bash, and setup.sh can install Java through brew, winget, apt, or dnf, including sudo on Linux.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad auto-trigger phrases for mobile testing and then provides shell-heavy setup/run paths, including auto-install behavior, without strong scoping or confirmation language for high-impact setup steps.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script writes a disclosed ~/.maestro/activate.sh helper and installs under ~/.maestro, with no cron/service/backdoor behavior found, but it can also invoke privileged package-manager installs when Java is missing.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The Maestro, emulator, adb, APK install, and YAML-flow guidance is coherent with React Native/Expo E2E testing; the main concern is the installer authority used to reach that goal.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing or running setup. Prefer installing Maestro from a pinned, verified release instead of curl | bash, run setup as an unprivileged user, approve any sudo/package-manager steps deliberately, and avoid copying the CI example until the installer and third-party actions are pinned and verified.
llm.findings:
[T03] expected: Accepted as a material concern: the artifact really does document and implement unverified remote installer execution for Maestro locally and in CI; this is purpose-related but under-scoped and mutable after review.
[SC2] expected: Accepted in context: installing Maestro is expected for this skill, but curl-pipe-to-bash without pinning, checksum, signature, or review is not a proportionate installation mechanism.
[TM2] expected: Accepted only for the curl | bash cases as the same installer concern; the apt-get update && sudo apt-get install sequence is ordinary package-manager chaining, not independent evidence of abuse.
[PE2] expected: Accepted as a user-review concern because setup.sh may run sudo apt/dnf installs for Java, though this is disclosed and aligned with prerequisites rather than hidden privilege escalation.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted as supporting context: the artifact is shell-heavy and lacks explicit tool/permission scoping metadata beyond documentation.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Partly accepted: the broad trigger language is related to the skill's intended audience, but it can route generic mobile-testing requests into instructions that include installation and emulator control.
[RP1] expected: Downgraded: the npx expo start references are local Expo authoring guidance, not a material MCP rug-pull issue in this artifact.
[RA2] expected: Downgraded: writing ~/.maestro/activate.sh is disclosed environment setup for explicit sourcing and is not evidence of unauthorized session persistence.
